title: Articles: A, An, The and Zero Article
summary: Select articles using countability, first mention, and shared reference.
learningObjectives: Use a/an for singular countable nouns introduced for the first time.
Recognize general plural and uncountable nouns without an article.

explanation.heading: Indefinite articles
explanation.body: A/an introduces one nonspecific singular countable noun; the choice follows sound, not spelling.
explanation.example: We need an oscilloscope and a USB cable.

explanation.heading: Definite article
explanation.body: The identifies something understood by the listener, including a second mention.
explanation.example: I found a sensor. The sensor was faulty.

explanation.heading: Zero article
explanation.body: General plural and uncountable nouns often have no article.

right.label: The
right.example: The software on this board needs testing.

examples.note: An is chosen before a vowel sound.

examples.sentence: Could you pass me the screwdriver on the table?
examples.note: The phrase identifies a particular tool.
An abstract uncountable noun is used generally.

commonMistakes.why: Singular countable occupations require a determiner.
New starts with a consonant sound.

studyTips: When unsure, ask whether the noun is singular and countable.
Check whether the listener can identify the particular thing.

exercises.feedback: Embedded begins with a vowel sound.

exercises.prompt: I found a connector. ___ connector was damaged.
exercises.feedback: Second mention makes the connector identifiable.

exercises.prompt: ___ information in this email is confidential.
exercises.feedback: The following phrase identifies specific information.
USB starts with the /juː/ consonant sound.
A singular countable noun first mentioned takes a.

exercises.prompt: I checked ___ report you sent me.
exercises.feedback: The relative clause identifies the report.
Experienced begins with a vowel sound.

exercises.prompt: This is ___ first test of the day.
exercises.feedback: Ordinals such as first normally use the definite article.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: She is electrical engineer.
exercises.feedback: A singular countable job title needs an article.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I need an USB cable.
Correct the sentence: We ordered a equipment yesterday.
Correct the sentence: He sent me report you requested.
acceptedAnswers: He sent me the report you requested.
exercises.feedback: The identifying clause specifies which report.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that you bought a new laptop yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: I bought a new laptop yesterday.
Yesterday I bought a new laptop.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use a with the singular countable noun laptop.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that the sun is shining.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use the for something unique in this context.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say that you need an umbrella.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use an before a vowel sound.
